# Workflow Supervisor 1.0.0

Released 2026-07-13.

Version 1.0 turns Workflow Supervisor from an eight-skill workflow framework into one small, explicit verification skill. The default path is now direct execution with no workflow artifact. Tracking and delegation are loaded only when they materially improve resume safety, independence, or isolation.

## Distribution Note

This is the GitHub source release. Its workflow attaches the verified npm-format tarball, `SHA256SUMS`, a CycloneDX `sbom.cdx.json`, and `provenance.intoto.json`. npm registry publication is a separate maintainer action and will happen later. Before installing from npm, check:

```bash
npm view workflow-supervisor version
```

Do not assume the registry carries `1.0.0` until that command says so.

The provenance statement records the tagged source commit, workflow run, builder environment, and tarball SHA-256. It is not npm registry provenance or a cryptographic signature; verify the attached checksums for downloaded assets.

## Native Plugin Invocation

The repository root is a Codex plugin: `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` points to the canonical root `skills/` directory. Invoke it explicitly as:

```text
$workflow-supervisor
```

For Claude Code, the repository root is a marketplace. `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` points to the actual plugin in `plugins/claude`. Invocation depends on how the skill was installed:

```text
Direct .claude/skills install:  /workflow-supervisor
Marketplace plugin install:     /workflow-supervisor:workflow-supervisor
```

## What Changed

- One discoverable `workflow-supervisor` skill replaces the seven companion skills and old profile framework, with host-native invocation shown above.
- Three proportional routes replace the old modes:
  - `direct`: no added state
  - `tracked`: one compact ledger when progress must survive a pause
  - `delegated`: one compact contract and validated result per worker
- Node.js 22 or newer is now required.
- `DelegationContractV1` is the preferred strict JSON worker input.
- `WorkerResultV1` removes wrapper-owned and duplicated fields from model output; the CLI normalizes it to `WorkerReportV1`.
- Built-in adapters use a provider-intersection transport schema accepted by Codex and Claude Code. The wrapper normalizes transport placeholders and then applies the stricter canonical `WorkerResultV1` runtime rules; provider schema acceptance alone cannot produce PASS.
- `delegate --preview` exposes exact prompt bytes, schema bytes, estimated tokens, command, and guard coverage before a model is launched.
- `context-budget` exposes exact profile byte counts and configured limits.
- Non-PASS delegation exits `2` by default. `--soft-exit` is the explicit opt-out.
- Worker processes receive a minimal environment. Credential forwarding requires exact variable names and matching explicit contract authority.
- Terminal output is accepted only from a direct result, Claude's successful structured-output carrier, or the final Codex agent-message carrier; command logs and stderr are never promoted to PASS evidence.
- The workspace guard covers embedded repositories, registered submodules, Git control state, and escaping symlinks across the full watched repository root.
- Forwarded credential values are scrubbed from untrusted text and diagnostics without rewriting trusted IDs, status/verdict enums, or validated paths; reserved protocol-value collisions fail before launch.
- Process execution is bounded by timeout and output size, cleans the owned process tree, waits for quiescence, and reports platform limitations.
- Install, upgrade, doctor, and uninstall use ownership manifests, target locks, checksum checks, and transactional replacement.
- Published Codex and Claude Code installs from `0.1.0` through `0.3.0` migrate with their original checksum/context rules; old `.gitignore` provenance is handled conservatively.
- Claude user installs and delegated subprocesses honor the documented `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` override.
- The Claude adapter disables skills and configured MCP servers but deliberately avoids `--bare` so normal OAuth/keychain authentication remains available.
- CI covers Ubuntu on Node.js 22, 24, and 26, plus macOS and Windows on Node.js 24. A separate package gate installs the generated tarball into a fresh npm consumer, verifies its version, and validates the installed artifact.

## Why It Is Better Than A Large Prompt Pack

A strong prompt remains the right tool for ordinary work. V1 no longer makes models carry an eight-skill catalog or repeated workflow instructions to do a simple edit.

Workflow Supervisor earns its overhead when a caller needs machine-checkable acceptance IDs, default-deny write scope, independent worker output, wrapper-owned mutation evidence, credential filtering, deterministic exit behavior, or a reproducible install lifecycle. It is a verification boundary around delegation, not a claim that extra prompting makes a new model smarter.

## Migration

Preview an existing managed install before replacing it:

```bash
workflow-supervisor upgrade --agent all --scope project --project . --dry-run
workflow-supervisor upgrade --agent all --scope project --project .
```

The upgrade removes manifest-owned 0.x companion skills only after checking for local modifications. Back up custom installed files before using `--force`.

If `0.1.0 --agent all` installed the retired OpenCode or HermesAgent copies, clean those backed-up targets with the exact old CLI before v1 migration. V1's `--agent all` covers only Codex and Claude Code. The migration guide gives the exact commands and stop conditions.

New contracts should be rebuilt as DelegationContractV1 rather than mechanically renaming DossierV1 fields. The legacy `validate-dossier`, `--dossier`, and legacy raw WorkerReportV1 paths remain available with deprecation warnings for migration.

See the [v1 migration guide](https://github.com/NikolaCehic/workflow-supervisor/blob/v1.0.0/docs/migrating-to-v1.md).

## Trust Boundary

Workflow Supervisor validates and detects; it does not provide complete containment.

- Mutation checks are scoped to canonical `--cwd` and declared surfaces.
- The CLI does not automatically revert a violating worker.
- POSIX process-group cleanup cannot reach a descendant that deliberately creates another session or joins another group.
- Windows ancestry-based cleanup cannot prove termination of every previously detached descendant.
- Files, services, credentials, network access, and side effects outside the governed workspace remain controlled by native permissions and the operating system.

Use an OS-level sandbox or container when prevention matters.

## Before Using Live Delegation

Run the package and adapter gates against the environment that will execute workers:

```bash
npm run validate
workflow-supervisor context-budget --profile delegated
workflow-supervisor delegate-doctor --agent all --probe --require-pass
```

The live probe can consume provider quota or incur cost. Adapter compatibility depends on the locally installed and authenticated Codex and Claude Code CLIs.

The configured CI and release workflows verify the package and tarball, but they do not certify every provider CLI version, local authentication setup, filesystem, or detached-process behavior. Run the diagnostics again in the target environment.

Full details are in the [changelog](https://github.com/NikolaCehic/workflow-supervisor/blob/v1.0.0/CHANGELOG.md), [CLI reference](https://github.com/NikolaCehic/workflow-supervisor/blob/v1.0.0/docs/cli.md), and [portable delegation guide](https://github.com/NikolaCehic/workflow-supervisor/blob/v1.0.0/docs/portable-delegation.md).
